title: LeakyDSP: Exploiting Digital Signal Processing Blocks to Sense Voltage Fluctuations in FPGAs
problem: Cloud FPGA multi-tenancy enables power side-channel attacks; existing attacks rely on crafted circuits, but DSP blocks—abundant in modern FPGAs—remain unexploited as malicious sensors.
motivation: Multi-tenant FPGA clouds expose shared power networks to covert channels; leveraging available DSP blocks enables practical voltage-based side-channel attacks.
method: Proposes LeakyDSP, a malicious configuration of DSP blocks to sense fine-grained voltage fluctuations in FPGAs; DSP blocks are reconfigured as voltage sensors to detect colocated circuit activity and extract secrets.
key_novelty: First voltage-sensing side-channel attack using only DSP blocks as on-chip sensors in FPGAs.
contributions: DSP block configuration as voltage sensor achieving high sensitivity and placement robustness
AES key extraction from 25k-78k power traces using DSP-based sensing
Covert channel construction with 247.94 bit/s transmission rate

metrics.other: 25k-78k traces for full AES-128 key extraction

limitations: Not discussed—no analysis of detectability or mitigation strategies.
primary_theme: Voltage side-channel attack via DSP block reconfiguration
